chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from al-Hajjal, from Ali ibn Shajara, from Isa ibn Rashid, from a man from his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who holds the four sides of the coffin, Allah will forgive him forty major sins.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.السَّرِير: Coffin or bier used for carrying the deceased

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for carrying a coffin in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), linking the physical act of carrying the coffin to spiritual purification. The specific mention of 'four corners' (jawanib) underscores the communal responsibility in Shia funeral rites, where active participation in the burial process serves as a means to expiate forty major sins, reflecting the high status of honoring the deceased.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Al Hajjal, from Ali Bin Shajara, from Isa Bin Rashid, from a man from his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who grabs by the four sides of the coffin, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Forgive for him forty major sins’.
en.sarwar: 3. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from al-Hajjal from Ali ibn Shajarah from ‘Isa ibn Rashid from a man of his people who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘
If one lifts up all four corners of the coffin Allah forgives his forty major sins.’”
